accepted.sentence: Commercial fields are concentrated in warm tropical and subtropical regions, where year-round temperatures support continuous growth.
Even brief frost can injure these plants, making frost-free locations important for dependable cultivation.
They grow best in deep, fertile, well-drained soil; standing water around the roots can encourage disease.
In humid climates, ample rainfall supports rapid growth, while irrigation can help during prolonged dry spells.
Open, sunny sites favor vigorous growth, whereas dense shade can slow development and reduce yields.
Strong winds can shred the broad leaves or topple laden plants, so sheltered fields and windbreaks are useful.
Cooler conditions at higher elevations slow development, so commercial cultivation is generally concentrated at lower tropical elevations.
On small farms, these plants are sometimes integrated into mixed tropical plantings alongside crops such as coffee or cacao.
